key: Through all this world strode Visnu; thrice his foot he planted, and the whole Was gathered in his footstep’s dust.
s: Near the close of a hymn calling a round of gods to the rite, six verses praise Visnu, his strides and his highest place; Sāyaṇa, on 1.22.17, reads it of Visnu’s descent as Trivikrama, the three-strider, and Yāska, Nirukta 12.19, explains the three steps by two teachers’ views: earth, mid-air and heaven, or sunrise, the meridian and sunset.

evidence.words: विष्णुः त्रिविक्रमावतारधारी “इदं प्रतीयमानं सर्वं जगदुद्दिश्य "वि “चक्रमे विशेषेण क्रमणं कृतवान् … विष्णुस्त्रिधा निधत्ते पदं त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः समारोहणे विष्णुपदे गयशिरसीत्यौर्णवाभः … Thrice he plants liis foot, [for threefold existence]. 'On earth, in the intermediate space, and in heaven,' … On the mountain of sunrise, on the meridian, and on the mountain of sunset,' says Aurnavabha.
evidence.gloss: [Sāyaṇa:] Vishnu, bearing the Trivikrama descent (avatāra), strode in a special striding over this whole world that appears to us … [Yāska, Nirukta 12.19, in his Sanskrit as Sāyaṇa quotes it:] Vishnu plants his foot thrice, for threefold existence: on earth, in mid-air, in heaven, says Śākapūṇi; on Samārohaṇa, on Viṣṇupada, on Gayaśiras, says Aurṇavābha … [Yāska in Sarup’s English, OCR as printed, liis for his:] thrice he plants his foot, for threefold existence: on earth, in the intermediate space and in heaven … on the mountain of sunrise, on the meridian, and on the mountain of sunset, says Aurṇavābha.

reason: Both problems hold. (1) The context clause used the “turns to” formula; it now says what the six verses do: 1.22.16 to 1.22.21 in day.js praise Visnu’s strides (16 to 18), his works (19) and his loftiest place or station (20, 21), so “praise Visnu, his strides and his highest place” rather than the critic’s narrower “praise Visnu’s strides”. (2) Re-opened packet.js veda 2 --verse 1.22.17: the Nirukta 12.19 section (Sarup’s English, and Yāska’s Sanskrit as Sāyaṇa quotes it, nirukta 12.18 to 12.19) gives the three steps as earth, mid-air and heaven (Śākapūṇi) or the mountain of sunrise, the meridian and the mountain of sunset (Aurṇavābha); Sāyaṇa’s own gloss is the Trivikrama avatāra. Yāska reports these as two teachers’ views, so the sentence says he “explains the three steps by two teachers’ views” rather than giving either view to him as his own; Wilson’s note on 1.22.17 names the same disagreement. Two-commentator form, 58 words; the difference is named, not resolved. Sāyaṇa’s reading is kept, shortened (the dusty footprint clause dropped for the cap). src 142 characters, both named. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 1.22.17, at [21,17]); entry-check ok; all four evidence pieces re-found in the packet with the recheck matcher’s normalisation.
